description: ROUND-2 VERIFICATION: RESOLVED. lib/note_publish.sh now defines _note_redact_secrets() (lines 91-119): a two-pass python3 redactor that (1) redacts every cookie VALUE loaded from NOTE_COOKIES_FILE wherever it appears verbatim in sub-step output, and (2) generically redacts any 'cookie|session|token|auth'-keyed value via regex. EVERY non-zero-return branch in run_note_mode_a_publish (create failure line 232-234, missing-key line 238-240, eyecatch failure line 249-251, price failure line 257-259, verify non-PASS line 275-277) now pipes its raw captured output through _note_redact_secrets BEFORE re-emission to stderr -- confirmed by reading all 5 branches. tests/test-find005-redact-secrets-in-error-output.sh proves this with a synthetic secret-looking string ('SUPERSECRET_TOKEN_...') injected via a hermetic fake sub-step script: the secret does NOT appear verbatim in the final stderr output, a [REDACTED] marker appears in its place (proving redaction ran, not silent dropping), AND a control case with ordinary non-secret diagnostic text ('connection refused') passes through UNCHANGED (no over-redaction). Confirmed as a genuinely new, previously-failing (against pre-fix source, which had no _note_redact_secrets at all) test via the red-phase evidence log.

evidence.snippet:
create_out="$(note_create_rich_draft "$draft_path" "$title" 2>&1)"; create_rc=$?
if [ $create_rc -ne 0 ]; then
  create_out_redacted="$(printf '%s' "$create_out" | _note_redact_secrets)"
  echo "run_note_mode_a_publish: note_create_rich_draft failed: $create_out_redacted" >&2
  return 1
fi
